scenes.title: Peter Wason's 1968 UCL Tabletop: Four Cards ('E — K — 4 — 7') vs the 'Beer — Soda — 25 — 16' Reveal
scenes.era: 1968, University College London psychology seminar room

layout.description: Sunlit 1968 London wood-and-baize testing table displaying four large crisp white cards face-up in a row — **E**, **K**, **4**, **7** — beneath a printed placard reading 'RULE: If a card has a VOWEL on one side, it has an EVEN NUMBER on the other', with a parallel second row of concrete comparison cards ('BEER', 'SODA', '25', '16') beside it.

positions.who: Peter Wason (mannequin in 1968 British tweed jacket and tie)
positions.where: seated across the baize table holding one finger calmly beside card '7' as the volunteer confidently reaches for 'E' and '4'
reaching confidently toward 'E' and '4' — then freezing in astonishment as Wason flips '7' over to reveal a rule-shattering 'E' on its back!

props.name: four oversized double-sided Wason cards ('E', 'K', '4', '7')
props.period_detail: thick matte cardstock where flipping '7' reveals 'E' (rule broken!) while flipping '4' reveals 'K' (rule unbroken!)
props.physical_behavior: the exact 4-card puzzle viewers can play along with in 3 seconds

props.name: rule placard & '<10% Pick E & 7' vs '80% Pick Beer & 16' comparison tray
props.period_detail: second row showing identical logic as 'If Beer -> Over 21'

actions.verb_sequence: points confidently to 'E' and '4' -> Wason turns '4' over showing 'K' (harmless!) -> Wason flips '7' over revealing 'E' on the back, shattering the rule in one move
slides the parallel 'BEER / SODA / 25 / 16' row forward -> Student immediately points to 'BEER' and '16'

reactions.reaction: palms forehead laughing at how obvious '16 / 7' becomes in real-world terms
records the 90% abstract miss vs 80% concrete hit

scenes.wardrobe: 1968 British university tweed jacket, Oxford shirt, knit tie; collegiate wool jumper.
scenes.recognition_hook: Four cards — E, K, 4, 7 — fool 90% of university minds until you flip '7' and turn the exact same puzzle into a pub bouncer test.

key_visual.description: a 1968 wooden table with four large white cards labeled E, K, 4, and 7 beneath a vowel-even rule placard as a researcher flips card 7 to reveal a hidden E

scenes.title: Wason's '2 — 4 — 6' Confirmation Trap (1960)

layout.description: Bright desk where a volunteer writes endless 'Yes' triples ('8-10-12', '14-16-18') without ever testing '1-2-3'.

positions.where: beaming over a column of 'YES' checkmarks while completely wrong about the real rule ('any ascending numbers')

props.name: notepad of 'YES' triples vs untested '1-2-3' card
props.period_detail: shows why seeking 'Yes' locks in overly narrow myths

actions.verb_sequence: writes '20-22-24 -> YES!' and announces wrong rule -> Wason reveals '1-2-3' also gets YES

scenes.recognition_hook: Ten 'Yeses' in a row felt like genius proof — when one brave 'No' test ('1-2-3') would have revealed the truth in five seconds.

scenes.title: 1972 Postal-Stamp Envelopes: Instant 80% Mastery

layout.description: Tabletop with four real paper envelopes: Sealed, Unsealed, 50-Lire Stamp, 40-Lire Stamp.

positions.where: instantly flipping the Sealed envelope and the 40-Lire envelope to catch underpaid mail

props.name: four postal envelopes
props.period_detail: identical logic to E-K-4-7 solved effortlessly at >80% accuracy

actions.verb_sequence: flips Sealed + low-stamp envelope without hesitation

scenes.recognition_hook: Turn abstract letters into sealed envelopes with cheap stamps, and ordinary people suddenly reason like master logicians.

scenes.title: Flipping 'Card 7' on Your Own Pet Beliefs

layout.description: Sunlit desk with a two-column decision pad: 'Why I Might Be Right (Card 4)' vs 'What Would Prove Me Wrong? (Card 7)'.

positions.where: deliberately filling out the 'Card 7 Disproof Check' column before signing off

props.name: Card-7 Pre-Mortem Checklist
props.period_detail: forces active falsification search in everyday decisions

actions.verb_sequence: crosses out a one-sided search and runs the disconfirming query

reactions.reaction: catches a hidden flaw before launch

scenes.recognition_hook: Smart people don't win by piling up Card-4 'Yeses' — they win by flipping Card 7 before reality flips it for them.
